newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican subway project bid halted on complaint.
newsitem.headline: Mexican subway project bid halted on complaint.

text.p: Mexico's Comptroller General's Office (Secodam) suspended the bidding process for a contract to purchase 28 subway trains, estimated to be worth about $400 million, because of a complaint from one of the contenders, the Metro subway system said.
It said in a statement the process was suspended after the apparent losing bidder, Spain's Construcciones y Auxiliar de Ferrocarriles (CAF), complained about the decision.
"The Secodam gave instructions to the Collective Transport System (Metro) to suspend the auction process because the company presented its complaint," the Metro subway system said.
Media reports estimated the contract was for 252 train cars and their maintenance.
Sources among the bidders say the contract is worth about about $400 million, one of the largest put out to tender for the capital's extensive subway system in recent years.

The Metro said it had decided to accept the contract price bid from CAF competitor, Bombardier Concarril SA of Bombardier and GEC Alsthom Transporte de Mexico SA, a venture of France's Alcatel Alsthom and GEC Plc.
No formal announcement had yet been made on the contract's winner.

The other bidder was a consortium of CAF with Empresas ICA unit Industrias del Hierro SA, Japan's Mitsubishi Corp and MDM Metromex SA. The Metro said its bid did not comply with the technical requirements.
Secodam refused to comment on the suspension or the fate of the purchase contract.
